title: probing-sandwich-curation-notes-diane-park-2026-07-18
content:
Quick concept: 

Probing Sandwich (working name) — a light, repeatable eval pattern for catching subtle context-dependent regressions after quantization/kv-eviction changes. Want something between a toy probe and an expensive human eval: cheap to run on CI, sensitive to ordering/context drift, and gives an actionable failure signal (not just score drop).

Why: recent infra tweaks (kv eviction heuristics + low-bit kernel swap) produced a few small but customer-visible hallucination shifts. We need a compact probe set that exercises: (1) long-prefix stability, (2) short local-context priority, (3) retrieval-to-generation handoff.

Core idea (sandwich):
- Top layer (context skin): synthetic but realistic long prefix (300–800 tokens) sampled from product transcripts (anonymized).
- Middle layer (target slice): a short, high-information prompt fragment (10–50 tokens) where the answer depends on either the prefix or a tiny retrieved doc. This is the sandwich filling — sensitivity to which signal wins indicates KV cache / retrieval interactions.
- Bottom layer (anchor): a short trailing prompt that checks for consistency when the model sees a follow-up question that references earlier tokens (e.g., pronoun resolution, numeric invariants).

Properties desired:
- Cheap to run: batchable locally on CPU for small models; run nightly on a 4-GPU smoke cluster.
- Deterministic-ish: use fixed sampling seeds for synthetic prefix generation; include a few canonical real transcripts as anchors.
- Interpretable failures: classify failure modes as: slot-loss (token-level mismatch), hallucinated-assertion (model invents new facts), drifted-priority (retrieval ignored / prefix ignored).

Three short paper summaries (notes):
1) "Attention with Linear Complexity" (arXiv:2102.04366) — takeaways: structured approximations are useful but can change effective receptive field; implication: if we ever swap in a low-compute attention kernel for a host of short sequences, run sandwich probes focusing on edge-case long prefixes. Implementation note: track activation patterns pre/post kernel swap on a small set of tokens (50–200).

2) "Mixing Retrieval and Cached KV" (arXiv:2302.08597) — takeaways: explicit gating between KV cache and retrieval reduces conflicts but requires tuning by sequence length distribution; for Redwood: propose a routing policy flag that biases retrieval when prefix length < X and KV when > Y. Sandwich probes can be parameterized across those thresholds.

3) Recent workshop talk (MLSys 2026 poster) on eviction heuristics — practical heuristics (time-decay + importance score) beat naive LRU in mixed workloads. But side-effect: priority changes cause subtle pronoun resolution regressions when important early tokens get evicted. Mitigation: add a small pinned-KV budget for named-entities detected in prefix. Experiment note: test pinned-KV of size 64 entries and measure sandwich failure rate.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Axis A: model variant (fp16 baseline, int8 quant, int4 experimental)
- Axis B: eviction policy (LRU, time-decay, score-prioritized)
- Axis C: retrieval bias (none, bias-to-retrieval, bias-to-cache)
- Metrics: sandwich-failure-rate, token-level KL on target slice, latency p95, tokens/sec cost estimate
- Run plan: small pilot (1 day) to prioritize combos, nightly regression (10 combos) for CI, weekly expanded (full matrix) for release gating.

Checklist / TODO: 
- [ ] Pull anonymized transcript samples (CS) — ask Rina for a 10k-token sample set, redact PII.
- [ ] Implement sandwich generator script (python) — make it export JSONL with seeds + metadata. Estimate: 1–2 dev days.
- [ ] Hook to existing lightweight-eval runner. If missing, wrap a simple loop over model variants + policies.
- [ ] Add classifiers for failure modes (heuristic-based first).
- [ ] Create dashboard card in Console (ops) showing sandwich-failure-rate over time and per-model.

Open questions / quick hypotheses: 
- H1: Small pinned-KV (32–128 items) reduces pronoun-related regressions by >=40% with <2% latency increase.
- H2: Int4 quantization interacts with eviction heuristics non-linearly; expect different optimal eviction policy for int4 vs fp16.
- H3: Retrieval bias parameter has a sweet spot near 0.2 for conversational transcripts where short recency matters more than deep prefix.

Notes for implementation details: 
- Use deterministic tokenizers (note: some tokenizers differ across runtimes) — pin tokenizer version in generator metadata.
- Ensure seeded sampling of long prefixes uses the same sharding logic as production log ingestion so distribution matches.
- Annotate each probe with provenance (product area: chat, doc-assistant, search) to track which customer flows are fragile.

Mini reading list for collaborators (to skim):
- "Efficient Transformers" survey (link saved in Slack pin) — quick brush for alternative kernels.
- ArXiv 2302.08597 (retrieval+kv) — above.
- Internal SRE note: eviction incident 2026-03-04 (redwood.slack link above) — read for real-world signal.

Slack blurb draft (to post in #llm-eval):
"Heads up: prototyping a lightweight 'sandwich' probe set to catch context-priority regressions after quant/eviction changes. Short pilot should give a low-noise signal we can run in CI. Tagging @Rina @Kaito for sample pulls. Will share generator + minimal dashboard by next Wed.

Questions for Rina/Kaito:
- Can CS share 10 anonymized transcripts by Mon?
- Do we have a preferred small-cluster to run the pilot (4xA10 or similar)?

Rough timeline:
- Thu: generator PR + sample JSONL
- Fri: pilot runs and quick dashboard mock
- Next Wed: CI integration (smoke)

Final: keep this deliberately small — we want a high signal-to-noise probe that devs will actually look at before merging infra changes."

Random link cache: 
- Retrieval paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.08597
- Efficient attention backbone: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.04366
- Internal issue for past eviction regression: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issue/1482

End notes: capture any surprising failure cases during pilot and add to a small canon of 'failed-sandwiches' (i.e., 10 canonical failure examples we can replay during PR review).

-- Diane
